record.program_name: County Affordable Housing Trust Fund (Section 20.234.010), established but uncapitalized
record.administering_agency: Mendocino County Board of Supervisors; to be administered by a nonprofit designated by the Board
record.typical_award_size: Section 20.234.010 (Ord. No. 4538, September 10, 2024) establishes an Affordable Housing Trust Fund to receive all funds collected under Chapter 20.234 (equity-sharing payments on density bonus for-sale units) and monies from other sources, administered by a Board-designated nonprofit and spent per the Housing Element to construct, rehabilitate or subsidize housing for extremely low through moderate income households, with an annual Board accounting. No deposits, designated administrator or awards were found in Board records.
record.affordability_requirement: Extremely low, very low, low and moderate income households; renter or owner housing.
record.next_deadline: No funding; watch the annual Board review required by the chapter and the 2027-2035 Housing Element for a capitalization source.
record.layering_notes: Mendocino County has no housing department: the Executive Office Grants Division administers state CDBG and HOME program income, Social Services is the administrative entity for the Mendocino County Homeless Services Continuum of Care (CA-509) and HHAP, Behavioral Health and Recovery Services holds BHSA, NPLH and bridge housing, Planning and Building Services handles density bonus and the Housing Element, and the Community Development Commission of Mendocino County (CDC, the housing authority) supplies vouchers and owns housing. The County repealed its inclusionary ordinance on September 10, 2024, has no housing trust fund money, no NOFA and no impact fee waiver; County capital help has come from state pass-through grants (CDBG-DR, Homekey) and small HOME program income balances. Ukiah and Fort Bragg run their own programs (Pass 3). mendocinocounty.gov, the Legistar web API client 'mendocino', mendocino.granicusideas.com and cdchousing.org all open normally. Confirmation needed on whether any balance exists; the 2024 code created the vehicle without a revenue stream, so treat it as a future possibility only. Source is Ordinance No. 4538 (Inland Zoning Code Update, adopted September 10, 2024, Legistar item 24-0848), Section 20.234.010; zoneomics carries the same text. A Legistar title search found no item designating an administrator or depositing funds.
eligible_project_detail: construct, rehabilitate or subsidize affordable renter or owner housing for extremely low to moderate income households (when funded)
record.audit_note: funding_type kept as other: the fund has no revenue stream, no balance and no designated administrator, so nothing is deployable; reclassify to loan or grant if the Board capitalizes it and sets terms. Source moved from the zoneomics mirror to the official ordinance on Legistar.
